Problem Identification: Build a lightweight Flask app to analyze TripAdvisor hotel reviews: 1) clean text, 2) cluster into high-level themes, 3) sentiment scoring, 4) expose /predict API and a minimal UI.
Data issues / EDA: Source in SQLite (data/clustering.db table tripadvisor_reviews) or CSV (data/sample_reviews_30.csv). Primary text: review_full. EDA: casing/punctuation/emojis; duplicates; short/empty rows; small demo CSV. Environment: missing NLTK corpora; restricted downloads.
ML Model: (A) BERT embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) + KMeans + labels; (B) TF-IDF + KMeans baseline for offline/demo. Auto-selects available artifacts; heuristic fallback if none.
Preprocess: Lowercase, remove non-letters, preserve negations, stopword removal, lemmatize. Safe fallbacks if NLTK corpora absent.
Issues Faced: Server not listening → ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED; Port conflicts/host binding mismatch; NLTK LookupError; Eager BERT import slowed/failed startup offline; Missing TF-IDF .pkl artifacts; Static cache served old UI; Analyze seemed unresponsive when server stopped; Sentiment misclassified for 'not good'/'not bad'/'best'.
Resolutions: Added /health + server.log; CLI flags --host/--port with fallback 3000→5000→8000; Waitress WSGI fallback on Windows; Default host 0.0.0.0; Fixed run-loop bug; Disabled NLTK downloads at import + robust fallbacks; Lazy BERT load; Built TF-IDF artifacts via src/build_tfidf_models.py; Cache-busting for CSS/JS and new /version; Added Clear button and polished UI; Replaced naive sentiment with lexicon + 2-word negation window, intensifiers/diminishers, 'but' contrast; Expanded positive/negative vocab.
How to Run: Install: pip install -r requirements.txt; Start: python app/app.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000 (try 5000/8000 if busy); UI: http://127.0.0.1:3000/ ; Health: /health ; Version: /version; Train baseline: python src/build_tfidf_models.py (creates models/kmeans_model.pkl, models/tfidf.pkl); Optional BERT: python src/train_embeddings.py --algo kmeans --clusters 5; Test API: python src/ping_predict.py
